chapters.title: Chapter 1: ITR Basics: What, Why and Who Must File

lessons.title: What Is an Income Tax Return? FY, AY and the Language of Filing

body.text: Paying tax and filing a return are two different things. Your employer and your bank may already have paid most of your tax for you. Filing is how you tell the government the full story, settle the difference, and get back anything you overpaid.

markDefs.definition: A form filed with the Income Tax Department declaring your income for a year, the deductions you claim, the tax already paid, and the final tax due or refund owed.

children.text: Every July, crores of Indians log in to the income tax portal and file an
Income Tax Return

, or ITR. Most first-timers get stuck before they even start, not on the maths, but on the vocabulary. FY, AY, tax year, Form 16, 26AS, AIS, e-verify. This lesson fixes that. By the end, you will be able to read any tax notice, portal screen or payslip footnote and know exactly which year and which document it is talking about.
What an ITR Actually Is

An ITR is a self-declaration. You report what you earned during the year from every source, the deductions you are entitled to, and the tax that has already been paid on your behalf through TDS or by you directly. The return then works out one of three results: you owe more tax, you are square, or the government owes you a refund.

The legal basis is Section 263 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 139 of the Income-tax Act, 1961). It lays down who must file, by when, and how late, revised and updated returns work. Returns are filed online on the Income Tax Department's e-filing portal. Paper returns are effectively a thing of the past for salaried individuals.

children.text: FY and AY: The Two-Year Label That Confuses Everyone

markDefs.definition: The 12 months from 1 April to 31 March during which income is earned. Under the Income-tax Act, 1961 this was also called the previous year.
Under the Income-tax Act, 1961, the 12 months immediately after the financial year, during which that year's income is assessed and the return is filed.

children.text: Indian income tax runs on a
Financial Year (FY)
from 1 April to 31 March. You earn income in the FY. Under the 1961 Act, that income is then assessed in the following year, called the
Assessment Year (AY)
. The AY is always one year ahead of the FY. Earn in FY 2025-26, file for AY 2026-27.

Take Priya, a software engineer at Infosys in Bengaluru. Her salary credited from April 2025 to March 2026 is FY 2025-26 income. When she files in July 2026, the portal, her Form 16 and her CA will all call it AY 2026-27. Same income, two labels, depending on whether you are talking about when it was earned or when it is assessed.

columns.label: Financial Year (FY 2025-26)
points: The year you earn salary, interest, rent and gains
The year your employer deducts TDS every month
The year in which you must make tax-saving investments to claim them
Called the previous year in the 1961 Act

columns.label: Assessment Year (AY 2026-27)
points: The year you file the return for FY 2025-26 income
The year the department processes it and issues refunds
The label you select on the e-filing portal for this return
Discontinued as a term under the 2025 Act

body.title: Pick the Right Label
body.question: Rohan, a teacher in Jaipur, receives FD interest from SBI in January 2026. When he files his return for this interest, which year will he select on the e-filing portal?
body.explanation: January 2026 falls in FY 2025-26, which runs from 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026. The matching assessment year is always one year ahead, so AY 2026-27. Tax Year 2026-27 is the new Act's label for income earned from April 2026 to March 2027, which is a different year altogether.

children.text: The New Act Simplifies This: Say Hello to the Tax Year

markDefs.definition: Under Section 3 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, the 12-month financial year starting 1 April in which income is earned. It replaces both previous year and assessment year.

children.text: The Income-tax Act, 2025 came into force on 1 April 2026 and replaced the 1961 Act. One of its most practical changes is the
tax year

, defined in Section 3. The two labels collapse into one: the year you earn the income is the tax year, and the term assessment year is dropped. Income earned from April 2026 to March 2027 is simply Tax Year 2026-27.

Here is the catch for anyone filing in 2026. Income earned in FY 2025-26 was earned while the 1961 Act was in force, so that return still follows the 1961 Act and still uses the AY 2026-27 label. The tax year label takes over from the returns you file in 2027 onwards. For the next couple of years you will see both sets of terms, so you need to be fluent in both.

body.caption: Which Label Applies to Which Income

body.text: A simple rule that works under both laws: find the 1 April to 31 March window in which the money was earned. That window is the FY, and under the new Act it is also the tax year. Only the old AY label points to the year after.

body.title: Translate to the New Act
body.textWithBlank: Ananya earns a bonus from HDFC Bank in November 2026. Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, this income belongs to Tax Year ___.
body.explanation: November 2026 falls in the window from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027. Under the 2025 Act, that window is Tax Year 2026-27. She will file the return for it in 2027.

children.text: The Filing Vocabulary You Will Use in Every Lesson
These terms come up on every screen of the portal. Flip through them until you can define each one without looking.

cards.definition: Permanent Account Number. Your 10-character tax identity. Every return, TDS entry and refund is tracked against it.
Tax Deducted at Source. Tax cut by the payer (employer, bank, tenant) before paying you and deposited against your PAN.
The certificate your employer issues by 15 June, showing your salary, exemptions and TDS deducted for the year.
The department's statement of tax credits against your PAN: TDS, TCS, advance tax and self-assessment tax paid.
Annual Information Statement. A wider record of your financial transactions: interest, dividends, share sales, mutual fund redemptions and more.
The last date to file your return without a late fee. 31 July 2026 for most salaried individuals filing for FY 2025-26.
A return filed after the due date but within the allowed window, with a late fee.
Balance tax you pay yourself before filing, when TDS and advance tax fall short of your final liability.
Confirming your filed return, usually through an Aadhaar OTP. A return that is not verified within the time limit is treated as never filed.
Excess tax paid through TDS or advance tax, returned by the department to your pre-validated bank account after processing.

children.text: What a Return Calculates: One Worked Example
Every ITR, however complicated, runs the same basic sequence. Add up your income, subtract what the law allows, apply the tax rates, then compare the result with the tax already paid.

body.latex: \text{Tax Payable or Refund} = \text{Tax on Total Income} - \text{Rebate} + \text{Cess} - (\text{TDS} + \text{Advance Tax})
body.caption: A positive result means you pay the balance before filing. A negative result is your refund.

children.text: Meet Sneha, an analyst at TCS in Pune. In FY 2025-26 she earns a salary of ₹9,00,000 and ₹60,000 interest on an FD with ICICI Bank. She is in the new tax regime, the default. Her employer deducted no TDS on salary, because her taxable salary was within the rebate limit. The bank, however, deducted ₹6,000 TDS on the interest, because once a non-senior citizen's interest from one bank crosses ₹50,000 in a year, TDS of 10% applies to the full amount.

body.caption: Sneha's Return for FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27), New Regime

cells: Add: FD interest (income from other sources)
Tax as per new regime slabs
Less: rebate (total income up to ₹12 lakh)
Less: TDS deducted by ICICI Bank

children.text: Because Sneha's total income of ₹8,85,000 is within ₹12 lakh, the rebate wipes out the full ₹28,500 (the rebate is capped at ₹60,000 in the new regime). Cess is 4% of tax after rebate, so it is also zero. The entire ₹6,000 the bank deducted comes back to her, but only if she files.

body.label: The Refund Only Exists on Paper Until You File
body.context: The bank deposited Sneha's TDS against her PAN. The department will not return it on its own. Filing the ITR is the claim.

body.title: Your Turn: Work Out the Refund
body.prompt: Arjun, who works at Tata Motors in Pune, has total income of ₹10,50,000 for FY 2025-26 under the new regime, after the standard deduction. His employer deducted ₹15,000 TDS on salary, and he paid no advance tax. Using the same sequence as Sneha's example, how much refund is Arjun due?
body.explanation: Tax on slabs: nil up to ₹4 lakh, 5% on ₹4 lakh (₹20,000), 10% on ₹2,50,000 (₹25,000), total ₹45,000. Total income is within ₹12 lakh, so the rebate removes all ₹45,000. Tax after rebate and cess is ₹0. His employer over-deducted, so the full ₹15,000 TDS comes back as a refund when he files.

children.text: One Return, Several Forms
There is no single ITR form. The department notifies different forms depending on who you are and where your income comes from. Chapter 4 covers each in detail. For now, just know the landscape.

body.caption: ITR Forms for Individuals at a Glance

cells: Residents with total income up to ₹50 lakh from salary, one house property, other sources, and limited long-term equity gains
Individuals and HUFs with no business income, including capital gains beyond ITR-1 limits or foreign assets
Salaried employee who sold shares on Zerodha
Individuals and HUFs with income from business or profession
Futures and options trader, consultant keeping full books
Residents with presumptive business or professional income and total income up to ₹50 lakh

body.label: Income Tax Department e-Filing Portal
body.description: The official portal where you register with your PAN, download Form 26AS and AIS, file your ITR and track your refund. Bookmark this and ignore look-alike sites.

body.text: Clicking Submit on the portal is not the end. Your return must be e-verified, usually with an Aadhaar OTP, within 30 days of filing. Skip this and the return is treated as if it was never filed, which means no refund and possibly a late fee. Chapter 5 walks through e-verification step by step.

body.title: The Dropdown Dilemma
body.scenario: Karthik joined Wipro in Chennai in October 2025. In June 2026 he logs in to the e-filing portal for the first time to file for the salary he earned between October 2025 and March 2026. The Assessment Year dropdown shows AY 2026-27 and AY 2025-26. A colleague tells him to pick AY 2025-26, because the salary was earned in 2025. Another says there is no AY any more because the new Act came in from April 2026.
body.prompt: Which option should Karthik select, and what is wrong with each colleague's advice?
body.modelAnswer: Karthik should select AY 2026-27. His salary from October 2025 to March 2026 falls in FY 2025-26, and the assessment year under the 1961 Act is always one year ahead of the financial year. The first colleague is confusing the calendar year of the salary with the assessment year: AY 2025-26 is for income earned from April 2024 to March 2025, before Karthik even joined. The second colleague is half right: the Income-tax Act, 2025 did replace AY with the tax year from 1 April 2026, but that change applies to income earned from April 2026 onwards. Income for FY 2025-26 is still filed under the 1961 Act with the AY 2026-27 label.

body.title: Before You Move to the Next Lesson
steps: Write down the FY and AY for the return you are going to file in 2026
Find your PAN card and check that the name matches your bank account and Aadhaar
Open the e-filing portal at incometax.gov.in and check whether you already have a login
Ask your HR team or payroll portal when Form 16 for FY 2025-26 will be available
Note 31 July 2026 in your calendar as the due date for ITR-1 and ITR-2

points: An ITR is a self-declaration of your income, deductions and taxes already paid, which works out whether you owe more tax or are due a refund
Returns are governed by Section 263 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 139 of the 1961 Act) and filed online on the e-filing portal
Under the 1961 Act, income is earned in the Financial Year and assessed in the Assessment Year, one year later: FY 2025-26 income is filed as AY 2026-27
The Income-tax Act, 2025, in force from 1 April 2026, replaces both labels with a single tax year, starting with Tax Year 2026-27
Returns filed in 2026 for FY 2025-26 still follow the 1961 Act, with a due date of 31 July 2026 for ITR-1 and ITR-2 filers
TDS already deducted from your income is only refunded when you file, and a return only counts once it is e-verified

Due dates, slab rates, rebate limits and TDS thresholds reflect the position for FY 2025-26 at the time of writing and are subject to change by the Finance Act or CBDT notifications. Verify current requirements on the Income Tax Department's portal or consult a qualified tax professional before filing.
